original_title: Synthesis and molecular docking of novel pyrazole, pyrimidine, and pyridine derivatives as potent antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anticancer agents
title: One chalcone scaffold, three heterocycle families, pick your antibacterial
blurb: A set of pyrazoles, pyrimidines, and pyridine/oxazinone derivatives built off a shared chalcone scaffold, screened for antibacterial, antibiofilm, and anticancer activity with docking and qRT-PCR to guess at mechanism. Pyrazoles 3-5 and oxazinone 13 came out strongest against S. aureus, the kind of broad-hit result that wants a second lab before you believe it.

original_title: Getting Around the Intrinsic Errors of Density Functional Theory Calculations in Electrocatalysis
title: DFT's gas-phase error problem has a cheap fix: stop referencing gas-phase species
blurb: Reference adsorption energies and barriers to surface-bound intermediates instead of molecular gas-phase species, and the usual DFT gas-phase error cancels out. Shown for OH adsorption in oxygen reduction, referenced to both Pt(111) and the Sabatier volcano apex, and for nitrogen reduction barriers. No new functional needed, just a smarter reference point.

original_title: A Light-Controlled DNA Nanoclaw Machine: Integrated Multiplexed Recognition, Spatiotemporally Programmable Therapy, and Real-Time Electrochemical Signaling for Precision Receptor Regulation
title: A light-gated DNA claw that only grabs cells wearing all three badges
blurb: A DNA nanodevice that checks for a triple-marker signature before switching on, then delivers light-triggered therapy and reports back electrochemically in real time. The multivalent, triple-marker gating is the point: a way around the usual problem that receptor targets are never expressed on just one cell type.

original_title: HPLC column recommendation for separating four closely related diastereomers
title: HPLC column recommendation for separating four closely related diastereomers

original_title: Overheated grill rack turns bright blue, why?
title: Overheated grill rack turns bright blue, why?
blurb: The above aluminum grill rack was overheated and partially melted. In the process, its formerly black coating turned bright blue. What is the chemistry involved in this? Any strongly-coloured compound subject to enough heat to melt aluminum (660˚C) is almost certainly inorganic, yet I can't offhand think of an inorganic compound without some metallic ions I wouldn't want to eat a lot of that would be a colour this vibrant. (The latter is probably due to my not being a chemist.) Anyhow, what is the probable chemistry going on here?

original_title: Differential Chemoselectivity of Homobifunctional and Monofunctional Maleimide Reagents for Bioconjugation
title: Multivalent maleimides don't play by monovalent rules
blurb: Thiol-maleimide chemistry is well understood for the standard single-maleimide reagent, but stack two maleimides on one linker for a multivalent bioconjugate and the chemoselectivity apparently shifts in ways that haven't been mapped out. Worth knowing before you assume a homobifunctional linker behaves like two monovalent ones taped together.

original_title: Reducing renal radioactivity of radiolabeled tetravalent RGD peptides via cleavable linkers for targeted radionuclide therapy.
title: Trimming kidney dose out of tetravalent RGD radiotherapy
blurb: Tetravalent RGD peptides for targeted radionuclide therapy tend to dump a lot of radioactivity in the kidneys, and this one tests cleavable linkers to knock that renal retention down.

original_title: Xcellon Acquires 40,000 Sq ft Maryland Facility from NextCure to Deliver a cGMP-Ready CRDMO for ADCs - BioBuzz
title: Xcellon turns NextCure's old Maryland building into an ADC plant
blurb: Xcellon bought the 40,000 sq ft facility off NextCure to stand up a cGMP-ready CRDMO for antibody-drug conjugates. Contract manufacturing capacity growing by way of somebody else's real estate.

original_title: Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry and Collision Induced Unfolding Distinguish Tryptophan and Methionine Oxidation in Intact Monoclonal Antibodies with Correlated Solution Stability Shifts
title: IM-MS tells tryptophan oxidation from methionine oxidation in intact mAbs
blurb: Ion mobility-mass spec plus collision-induced unfolding can pick apart Trp versus Met oxidation in a whole antibody, and the unfolding shifts track with real solution-stability changes measured separately. A biophysical readout for degradation pathways that used to be harder to tell apart.

original_title: Protocol for proteomic profiling of hypusinated protein candidates using a clickable spermidine probe.
title: A clickable spermidine probe for fishing out hypusinated proteins
blurb: A STAR Protocols method for proteomic profiling of hypusination candidates using a clickable spermidine probe. A protocol to run rather than a result to weigh.

original_title: STAT+: In surprise decision, FDA rejects radiopharma therapy expected to rival Novartis treatment
title: FDA rejects a radiopharma therapy that was set up to rival Novartis
blurb: Manufacturing issues, not efficacy, sank this one at the FDA, per STAT, and it was shaping up as real competition for Novartis's treatment. A CMC failure, not a clinical one, which is its own kind of setback.

original_title: In surprise decision, FDA rejects radiopharma therapy expected to rival Novartis treatment - STAT
title: Same Novartis-rival radiopharma, rejected again in the retelling
blurb: The wire version of the same STAT story: FDA turned down a radiopharmaceutical therapy that had been positioned against Novartis, over manufacturing problems.

original_title: Targeting Adaptive and Innate Immune Responses with Covalent Aptamers
title: Covalent aptamers turn anti-biotin CAR T cells into an on-demand kill switch
blurb: Aptamers against PTK7 and cMet get electrophile handles that covalently dump biotin onto the target protein, tagging it for universal anti-biotin CAR T cells to lyse. One version carries a cleavable electrophile too, so the tag looks switchable rather than permanent.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Development of a Fluorescent Probe for Real-Time In Vivo Imaging of Cysteine Dynamics in a Mouse Model of Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Acute Lung Injury
title: A near-infrared probe that watches cysteine spike during lung injury, live
blurb: HD-Cys is an activatable hemicyanine dye that turns on near-infrared when it hits cysteine, and the authors ran it in vivo in an LPS-induced acute lung injury mouse model after validating it in BEAS-2B cells. Detection limit down at 160 nM with a linear response.

original_title: Assembly-formed bioorthogonal chimeric artificial receptors enable high-contrast fluorescence imaging of tumors
title: Building the tumor's own receptors, then imaging them
blurb: Instead of relying on whatever biomarker density a tumor happens to have, this assembles bioorthogonal chimeric receptors directly onto the tumor surface, raising effective receptor density and fluorophore binding for a sharper tumor-to-normal signal. Works around the low-biomarker ceiling that usually caps receptor-targeted imaging probes.

original_title: Neutral Backbone Modifications Enhance the Pharmacokinetics and Biodistribution of Antibody–Oligonucleotide Conjugates with High Drug-to-Antibody Ratios
title: Fixing the DAR-vs-biodistribution tradeoff in antibody-siRNA conjugates
blurb: High-DAR, TfR1-targeted antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates normally clear from plasma fast, dump into the liver, and skip muscle. Swapping in neutral backbone chemistry on the oligo apparently fixes that mismatch, so you can stack more siRNA per antibody without losing the tissue reach you wanted it for.

original_title: Dual‑targeted radioligand therapy with [(177)Lu]Lu‑DOTATATE plus [(177)Lu]Lu‑DOTA‑IBA for bone metastases from neuroendocrine neoplasms: a prospective pilot study.
title: Two Lu-177 payloads at once for neuroendocrine bone mets
blurb: A pilot study pairs the usual somatostatin-receptor-targeted Lu-177-DOTATATE with a bone-seeking Lu-177-DOTA-IBA, aiming both at bone metastases from neuroendocrine tumors in the same patients. Prospective but small, and no outcome numbers here, just the dual-targeting setup.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Photo‐Generated 1 O 2 Triggers In Situ RNA Crosslinking for High‐Contrast Tumor MRI and Effective Tumor Suppression
title: Light-triggered RNA crosslinking doubles as MRI contrast and tumor kill
blurb: A photoactivatable probe exploits how RNA-rich hepatocellular carcinoma cells are, and light sets off singlet oxygen that crosslinks the probe onto RNA in situ via furan chemistry. That locks the probe down, slowing its tumbling enough to light up on MRI, and the same reaction apparently wipes out the tumor. One photoreaction running the imaging and the therapy.

original_title: A Regioselective Azide–Alkyne Cycloaddition to 1,2,3-Triazole-4-carboxaldehydes, Polyheteroaryls, and Synthesis of Rufinamide
title: Metal-free triazole aldehydes, with a rufinamide synthesis to show for it
blurb: Propiolaldehyde made on the spot from propargyl mesylate reacts with azides with no metal catalyst, giving 1,2,3-triazole-4-carboxaldehydes with strong regioselectivity. They push those aldehydes into cascade reactions for heterobiaryls and heteroterphenyls, then scale it to grams and use it to build rufinamide, the actual epilepsy drug, which is the part worth remembering.

original_title: Acid-free activation of acyl hydrazides
title: Peptide ligation without the pH dance
blurb: Ferricyanide activates acyl hydrazides for peptide ligation right at neutral pH, cutting out the usual acidic activation and the pH adjustments that come with it. Small change, one less step to babysit mid-ligation.

original_title: SuFEx-Enabled Acyl Fluoride Chemistry for High-Concentration Minimal-Oligomerization Peptide Macrocyclization
title: Cyclizing peptides at 100 mM without the oligomer soup
blurb: Head-to-tail peptide macrocyclization normally forces dilute conditions or you get oligomers instead of your ring. A SuFEx-activated acyl fluoride biases the reaction toward closing on itself instead, staying clean up to 100 mM where the usual uronium and phosphonium coupling reagents just give you a pile of oligomeric junk. That's a real concentration jump, if it holds outside their test cases.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Synthesis, characterization and evaluation of [(169)Yb]Yb-labeled tailored hydroxyapatite nanospheres for potential application in nanobrachytherapy.
title: Yb-169 hydroxyapatite nanospheres for local radiotherapy
blurb: Hydroxyapatite nanospheres labeled with Yb-169, synthesized and characterized as a candidate for nanobrachytherapy. Straight synthesis-and-characterization work here, no efficacy data yet.

original_title: Role of Ionic Media in f–f Transitions, Stability, and the Structure of Ln(III) Coordination Compounds
title: The countercation you pick changes how your Er(III) complex behaves
blurb: Same Er(EDTA) hydroxide equilibrium, four different counterions swapped in (Na, K, guanidinium, tetramethylammonium), and the choice measurably shifts both complex stability and the f-f transition spectra, confirmed across XRD, UV-vis-NIR, 89Y NMR, and potentiometry. Worth it if you've been treating 'the ionic medium' as a footnote instead of a variable in lanthanide coordination chemistry.

original_title: Achieving Organocatalytic Control of P(III)-Centered Chirality for the Construction of P(III)/(V) Stereogenic Compounds
title: Building P-stereogenic compounds by treating phosphorus as the electrophile
blurb: P(III)/(V)-chiral building blocks usually come from transition-metal catalysis that uses phosphorus as a nucleophile. This flips it: an organocatalyst activates trivalent phosphorus directly as an electrophile for asymmetric substitution on chlorophosphites, building P(III)-stereogenic phosphinites with no metal involved. A genuinely underexplored angle in a field that's been metal-dominated.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dynamic Fluctuations Can Counteract Catalytic Inhibition and Enhance Catalytic Performance
title: A wobbling active site can outrun its own inhibitor
blurb: The standard line is that inhibition always throttles catalysis, but that's only been shown for static active sites. This theoretical work looks at dynamic catalysis, where the active site's properties fluctuate over time, and finds that the coupling between that fluctuation and the inhibition can actually cancel the inhibition out and boost performance. Theory only, nothing made here, but it's a real crack in an assumption everyone treats as settled.

original_title: Synthesis and Activity‐Based Protein Profiling Identifies Aldo‐Keto Reductase 1C3 as Target Protein of Myxoglucamides
title: First synthesis of myxoglucamides turns up a target nobody expected
blurb: Myxoglucamides had no reported bioactivity, so instead of screening for a phenotype the group synthesized the thing from scratch, the first total synthesis of this vinyl alpha-keto-gamma-amino acid glycolipopeptide, and went fishing with activity-based protein profiling. The hit is aldo-keto reductase 1C3, a cancer-relevant enzyme found before anyone had a phenotype to pin it on.

original_title: Predictive value of [99mTc]Tc-MAA SPECT/CT personalised dosimetry in 90Y radioembolization of hepatocellular carcinoma: a DOSISPHERE-01 ancillary study
title: How well does Tc-99m-MAA actually predict the Y-90 dose you get
blurb: DOSISPHERE-01 already showed personalized dosimetry beats standard dosing for Y-90 radioembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma. This ancillary analysis goes back through patients with both the pre-treatment Tc-99m-MAA SPECT/CT and the post-treatment Y-90 imaging to check how well the predictive scan matches the dose actually delivered, using two segmentation methods. That's the number that decides whether the pre-treatment scan is worth trusting or just theater before the real dose.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Managing hematological toxicity in [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTATATE for NET patients: a national survey from the French group of endocrine tumors (GTE) on the clinical need for harmonized monitoring strategies
title: France polls its own oncologists on how to watch for Lu-177-DOTATATE's blood toxicity
blurb: A national survey from the French group of endocrine tumors asking how centers are actually monitoring hematologic toxicity in Lu-177-DOTATATE patients, and whether there's enough agreement to write it down as one strategy. Running a harmonization survey usually means there isn't.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Expanding the Reactivity of Bifunctional Reagents: Photoinduced Metal-Free Access to Imino Carbonyl Compounds and Tetrahydrofurans
title: Alkoxy radicals go metal-free en route to imino carbonyls and THFs
blurb: N-oxime bifunctional reagents branch into two alkoxy radical pathways, beta-scission or cyclization onto a pendant alkene, then feed into metal-free 1,2-carboimination of activated alkenes under visible light with the organic photocatalyst 5CzBN. Same starting reagent, two different heterocycle classes depending on which pathway you let run.

original_title: Atroposelective Synthesis of Axially Chiral 4‐Aryl‐isoxazolo[5,4‐ b ]pyridines by Relay Catalysis
title: Chiral phosphoric acid and silver relay their way to axially chiral heterobiaryls
blurb: A relay catalysis setup pairing a chiral phosphoric acid with AgNO3 to run an atroposelective [3+3] cyclization cascade, building a new class of axially chiral 4-aryl-isoxazolo[5,4-b]pyridines. Heterobiaryl atropisomers are already prized in drug design; the list of ways to make them enantioselectively is still short, and this adds one.

original_title: Synthesis of C(CF3)Me2 Tetrahydropyridazines and Dihydropyrazoles via Radical Cascade and Mechanistic Studies by DFT Calculations
title: CF3-quaternary radicals cascade into tetrahydropyridazines and dihydropyrazoles
blurb: A metal-free radical cascade starting from 1,1-dimethyl-2,2,2-trifluoroethyl radicals, generated from the corresponding trifluoromethylated carboxylic acid, run against N-homoallyl or N-allyl aldehyde hydrazones to give fluorinated tetrahydropyridazines and dihydropyrazoles. 25 examples, moderate to good yields, no metal catalyst, and DFT to back up the mechanism they're proposing.

original_title: Rationally Designed Malonate-Derived Ligands Enable Copper-Catalyzed C–N Coupling via a Cu(I)/Cu(III) Mechanism
title: Malonamide ligands push Cu-catalyzed C-N coupling through a Cu(I)/Cu(III) cycle
blurb: Purpose-built, sterically bulky malonamide ligands let copper couple aryl and heteroaryl bromides with a broad range of amine nucleophiles, aryl, heteroaryl, alkyl, in high yield. They demonstrate it on actual API syntheses, which is the part that decides whether anyone bothers switching off palladium for this.

original_title: Inhibitors of IAP/XIAP enhance activity of sacituzumab govitecan
title: IAP inhibitors make sacituzumab govitecan hit harder in resistant breast cancer
blurb: Sacituzumab govitecan is already approved for breast cancer, but intrinsic and acquired resistance show up. Pairing it with IAP/XIAP antagonists like birinapant boosted antitumor activity in patient-derived xenografts and cell lines, birinapant notably alongside irinotecan-class chemo. Preclinical only, but a plausible fix for a drug that's already losing ground to resistance.
venue: JNCI Journal of the National Cancer Institute

original_title: Electrochemical Cross-Coupling of Electron-Deficient Olefins
title: Cross-coupling electron-poor olefins without them just homocoupling on you
blurb: Olefins with similar electron density tend to pair with themselves instead of each other, which is the whole problem with cross-coupling them. This electrochemical method breaks the tie by exploiting how differently each olefin interacts with a Lewis acid, effectively splitting their redox potentials apart so the cross product wins over homocoupling.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Pluvicto® Approved for PSMA-Positive mHSPC: Bringing Radioligand Therapy Earlier in the Disease Course - Oliver Sartor - UroToday
title: Pluvicto moves up a line, now cleared for PSMA-positive mHSPC
blurb: Oliver Sartor's take on the approval: Pluvicto no longer has to wait for castration resistance, it's now indicated in PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, earlier in the disease course than its original mCRPC approval.

original_title: Total Synthesis of (±)-Caryopincaolide A
title: First synthesis of caryopincaolide A, quaternary centers and all
blurb: The first total synthesis of this rearranged abeo-abietane diterpenoid, built by installing the aromatic ring early and closing the strained 5/6/6 core with an Fe(acac)3/PhSiH3 reductive alkene-enone coupling in 93% yield. Three contiguous all-carbon quaternary centers land in that one step, then carbonyl transposition and an ortho-quinone aromatization/lactonization sequence finish the job.

original_title: Engineered Dynamic Co2+ Sites Resolve the Complete Reaction Network for C(sp3)–H Oxidation
title: Making a catalyst's messy dynamics do something useful for once
blurb: Most operando studies just watch active sites shuffle during catalysis and shrug. This Co@Co3O4 core-shell catalyst runs on a reversible Co0/Co3+ to Co2+ solid-state redox equilibrium during toluene C(sp3)-H oxidation, and operando XAFS/XPS map the whole reaction network instead of one snapshot. The pitch is turning that dynamic behavior into a design rule rather than a footnote.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Generalization of Titanocene-Catalyzed Arylation of Epoxides through Radical Polar Crossover by Consecutive Paired Electrolysis
title: Pairing titanocene radical chemistry with an electrolysis cell to fix its rearomatization problem
blurb: Titanocene-catalyzed radical arylation of epoxides has always leaned on proton-coupled electron transfer for rearomatization, the fussy step. Splitting that into consecutive paired galvanostatic electrolysis separates the anodic oxidation from the proton transfer spatially, funneling things through a radical polar crossover instead. Mechanistically tidier, and it's what lets the method generalize beyond the original scope.

original_title: Monovalent Targeting Nanotag-Mediated Single-Molecule Counting by SP-ICP-MS
title: Counting single molecules by counting nanoparticles instead
blurb: SP-ICP-MS is already good at spotting one metal nanoparticle at a time, but wiring it up to count individual biomolecules has been the hard part. This uses a monovalent nanotag, one tag per target molecule, so each nanoparticle ping in the mass spec corresponds to one biomolecule counted. A lab tool for ultrasensitive bioanalysis, not a clinical assay yet.

original_title: Native Amine-Directed NiH-Catalyzed Markovnikov Hydroalkynylation of Unactivated Alkenes
title: Getting NiH hydroalkynylation to work with a free amine sitting right there
blurb: Free amines usually bind the nickel too well and wreck regioselectivity, so directing off them during Markovnikov hydroalkynylation of unactivated alkenes hasn't really worked. A diamine ligand fixes that, turning alkenyl amines and alkynyl bromides directly into β-, γ- and δ-aminoalkynes under mild conditions without protecting the amine first.

original_title: Enantioselective O/F Exchange of Sulfonimidoyl Fluorides with Alcohols
title: Sulfonimidoyl fluorides finally play nice with alcohols
blurb: Enantioselective chemistry at sulfur stereocenters has mostly been stuck on sulfonimidoyl chlorides, which either get reduced away under covalent activation or only tolerate phenols and diols under Lewis-acid catalysis. Swapping to the fluoride lets aliphatic alcohols do the O/F exchange enantioselectively, sidestepping both failure modes.

original_title: Air-Oxidizing, Solvent-Free Depolymerization of Plastic Waste to Produce Valuable Chemicals
title: Turning PET into terephthalic acid with just air and heat
blurb: No acid, no base, no solvent, no added hydrogen. An atomically dispersed Fe catalyst inside a zeolite oxidatively depolymerizes PET straight into 90.7% pure terephthalic acid at 260°C under oxygen, and it works with plain air too. About as low on reagent overhead as PET recycling gets, if the catalyst holds up outside a benchtop reactor.

original_title: Deoxygenative Amination of Unactivated Primary Alcohols Using Sulfonimidoyl Fluorides as an Ammonia Surrogate
title: An ammonia surrogate that turns primary alcohols into amines with the protecting groups already on
blurb: N-Boc-benzenesulfonimidoyl fluoride stands in for ammonia in deoxygenative amination of unactivated primary alcohols, going through a sulfonimidate ester from a SuFEx click and then an unprecedented [1,3] O-to-N rearrangement. The amines come out already wearing N-Boc and N-benzenesulfonyl groups that strip off easily, and the method tolerates a wide range of functional groups.

original_title: Synthetic Studies toward Neotatarine
title: Building toward neotatarine with a furan doing a [4+3] on itself
blurb: A modular route to a deoxy neotatarine congener that closes the ring via an intramolecular [4+3] oxyallyl cycloaddition of a furan, bookended by two cross-couplings from off-the-shelf building blocks. Short of the natural product itself so far, but built to be scaled and tweaked.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed Telomerization of 1,3-Butadiene Promoted by Triarylphosphines: Unveiling Mechanistic Details for Selective Production of 1-Methoxy-2,7-octadiene
title: Skipping palladium for butadiene telomerization, and explaining why the ligand matters
blurb: Butadiene plus methanol telomerization toward 1-octene precursors runs commercially on palladium, but this reroutes it through nickel and triarylphosphine ligands instead, cheaper and easier to recover. The real contribution is mechanistic: screening twelve phosphines to nail down how ligand structure steers selectivity toward 1-methoxy-2,7-octadiene specifically.

original_title: Substrate-Assisted Redox-Neutral Formal [4 + 3] Annulation of Alkynyl Aldehydes with 9,10-Phenanthrenequinones via N-Heterocyclic Carbene Catalysis
title: A redox-neutral [4+3] that builds dioxepinones without an oxidant
blurb: NHC catalysis pairs alkynyl aldehydes with 9,10-phenanthrenequinone, and the quinone does double duty as both annulation partner and internal oxidant, so no external oxidant is needed to close the seven-membered dioxepin-2-one ring. A neat way around the usual redox bookkeeping in NHC catalysis.

original_title: Learning millisecond protein dynamics from what is missing in NMR spectra
title: Reading protein dynamics from the NMR peaks that disappear
blurb: Peaks that vanish from an NMR spectrum usually just mean exchange broadening wiped out the signal, but this paper trains a model to read that absence itself as a readout of millisecond protein dynamics, turning a normal artifact into a measurement.

original_title: Study of Belantamab Mafodotin as Pre- and Post-autologous Stem Cell Transplant and Maintenance for Multiple Myeloma
title: Belantamab mafodotin gets a shot at maintenance duty around stem cell transplant
blurb: A Penn-run phase 2 testing belantamab mafodotin before and after autologous stem cell transplant, then as maintenance, in multiple myeloma. Worth remembering this is the antibody-drug conjugate that got pulled from the market once already over eye toxicity before its comeback, so the ocular side effects are the thing to watch here, not just response rates. Trial's active but no longer recruiting.

original_title: Energy Transfer Catalysis Enabled by Multichannel Through‐Space Charge Transfer TADF Photosensitizers: [2 + 2] Photocycloaddition to Cyclobutane‐Fused Phosphindole 3‐Oxides
title: A metal-free photosensitizer built to dodge the usual Ir/Ru trade-offs
blurb: Organic TADF sensitizers using multichannel through-space charge transfer to get around the weak absorption and short triplet lifetimes that usually plague carbonyl-based alternatives to Ir and Ru photocatalysts. They put it to work on [2+2] photocycloadditions to build cyclobutane-fused phosphindole 3-oxides. Heavy-atom-free triplet sensitization that doesn't need a noble metal is the actual selling point.

original_title: Geminal Difunctionalizations of Aliphatic Ketones and Aldehydes Enabled by Thioacetal Activation and Deep Electroreduction
title: Electroreduction turns dithioacetals into a handle for gem-difunctionalizing carbonyls
blurb: Dithioacetals work as disposable, redox-active activating groups that let deep electroreduction convert aliphatic ketones and aldehydes into dianion equivalents, deoxygenating them straight into gem-difunctionalized silanes, boronates, and germanes. The Faradaic control over chemoselectivity is the part worth noting, since the applied charge, not just the electrophile, decides what you get.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photocatalytic Aminocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkenes and Heteroarenes with CO2 toward β-Amino Acid Derivatives
title: CO2 as the amino acid's third carbon, straight off an unactivated alkene
blurb: A photocatalytic three-component reaction adds an amine and CO2 across unactivated alkenes and heteroarenes in one step to give beta-amino acids, using CO2 as the carboxyl source instead of a pre-installed carboxylic acid. First time this direct aminocarboxylation has been shown on unactivated alkenes, the harder substrate class to get to react.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Xcellon Biologics Acquires GMP Manufacturing Facility from NextCure, Becoming an End-to-End CRDMO for Next-Generation Bioconjugates and Complex Biologics - The Manila Times
title: Xcellon buys its way to owning the whole bioconjugate pipeline
blurb: Xcellon Biologics picks up NextCure's GMP manufacturing plant, turning itself into an end-to-end CRDMO covering next-gen bioconjugates and complex biologics rather than just running discovery work and shipping it out for manufacturing elsewhere.

original_title: Heterogeneous Palladium-Catalyzed Transfer Hydrogenation of Epoxide and Structurally Diverse Unsaturated Bonds at Room Temperature
title: A reusable Pd-MOF that hydrogenates epoxides at room temperature without additives
blurb: A UiO-67 MOF loaded with Pd runs transfer hydrogenation of epoxides to alcohols at room temperature using ammonia borane as the hydrogen source, no additives needed, and the catalyst is reusable. Same system also handles enones, N-heterocycles, azoarenes, and nitroarenes, so the scope runs well past epoxide opening.

original_title: Programmable Vacancy Topology in High-Entropy-Alloy-Inspired Multiprincipal Alloys Directs Ru-Centered Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
title: Programming vacancies into a five-metal alloy to tune Ru's neighbors
blurb: An H2-free, MOF-derived route to sub-4 nm MnFeRuCoNi nanoparticles that places vacancies specifically next to the Ru sites, backed by a full characterization stack (PALS, EPR, EXAFS, XPS, XANES, NAP-XPS) confirming both the defect structure and the resulting Ru-to-water charge transfer. All in service of tuning alkaline hydrogen evolution through vacancy topology.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photocatalyzed Regioselectivity Trifluoromethylation and Sulfuration of Unactivated Alkenes with S -Aryl Trifluoromethanesulfonothioates (TTSA)
title: One reagent adds CF3S across unactivated alkenes photocatalytically
blurb: A trifluoromethanesulfonothioate reagent (TTSA) reacts with unactivated alkenes under photocatalysis to install both a trifluoromethylthio and sulfur group in one step, in high yields. Radical trapping, scrambling, cyclic voltammetry, and Stern-Volmer studies all point to a reductive quenching cycle, so this is more than just a yields paper.

original_title: Selenoxanthylium Salts─Organic Photocatalysts for Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
title: Swapping in selenium to catalyze with red light
blurb: Photoredox catalysts usually get pushed to lower energy by stretching out the π-system, but here they just drop a heavier chalcogen into the xanthylium core instead. Selenium redshifts absorption enough to run catalysis off 650 nm light, and the excited state keeps its locally-excited and charge-transfer character distinct rather than blurring together. A second lever for low-energy photocatalysis that doesn't require building a bigger scaffold.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Electrochemical Synthesis of β-Arylamino Ketones from Tertiary Anilines and Silyl Enol Ethers
title: Electrochemistry swaps out the metal for β-arylamino ketones
blurb: Tertiary anilines and silyl enol ethers coupled at the electrode, no metal catalyst or chemical oxidant needed, good yields across a decent substrate range. They also ran it in a continuous flow cell, which is the part that actually points toward scale rather than just a nice bench reaction.

original_title: TiO2-facet-dependent reconstruction of Pt nanoparticles during CO oxidation
title: Which TiO2 facet you pick decides what your Pt nanoparticles turn into
blurb: Same ~1.8 nm Pt particles, different anatase TiO2 facet underneath, different outcome: (001) spreads the Pt into a wetted layer with a large metal-support interface, while (101) keeps it balled up as compact cuboctahedra barely touching the support. That split isn't just a starting-state quirk, it also governs how the particles restructure once CO oxidation actually gets going.

original_title: Room-Temperature Oxidative Cyclization of Carboxylic Acids Promoted by Copper(II) Trifluoromethanesulfonate and Selectfluor
title: A one-pot fix for the lactones that won't cyclize cleanly
blurb: Cu(OTf)2, Selectfluor, and KOtBu turn carboxylic acids into γ- and δ-lactones at room temperature, but not cleanly for every substrate, some give a pile of overoxidized ketone instead. Rather than optimize that away, they just add NaBH4 and then aqueous HCl to the same flask and push the ketone byproduct back to the lactone. A rescue step baked into the procedure instead of a scope limitation.

original_title: Electronic states of diarylethene switch–gold nanocluster hybrids
title: Diarylethene switches wired to gold nanoclusters
blurb: Thin on detail, but the pairing is the idea: photoswitchable diarylethenes hybridized with gold nanoclusters to see how flipping one changes the electronic states of the other.

original_title: A concentration-independent paradigm rendering weak interactions inherently quantifiable
title: Measuring weak binding without drowning it in concentration
blurb: Millimolar-affinity interactions run a lot of cell biology but have resisted quantification because reading weak binding through bulk concentration means pushing concentrations past what's practically doable. The fix is ditching the century-old habit of reading everything through molecule number over volume, and measuring these interactions in a way that doesn't depend on concentration at all. If it holds up, a whole tier of "too weak to measure" interactions becomes tractable.

original_title: Experimental access to molarity's blind spot in macroscopic assays
title: Giving local molecular crowding its own experimental handle
blurb: Companion piece to the concentration-independent binding paper above: ordinary kinetics reads everything back through flask-scale molarity, even concepts like effective molarity that are supposed to capture local structure. This is the bench-compatible flip side, making local structure itself something you can directly vary and measure instead of folding it back into one bulk concentration number.

original_title: Beyond Simple Mimicry: Next‐Generation Geometric Architectures and Future Paradigms in Small‐Molecule and Macrocyclic Peptidomimetics
title: Peptidomimetics grows up from one-off tricks into an engineering discipline
blurb: A perspective arguing peptidomimetics has moved past motif-by-motif mimicry into systematic geometric design, linear repetition, convergent fusion, cyclization, aimed at converting peptide recognition surfaces into orally bioavailable small molecules. It's a review, not new data, but a useful map if you're trying to shrink a peptide hit into something druggable.

original_title: Stereodivergent Sequential One‐Pot/Two‐Step Photo‐Biocatalytic Cascade for the Synthesis of Enantioenriched 1‐Arylalkan‐1‐ols From α‐Methylstyrenes
title: Light does the cutting, an enzyme does the picking
blurb: A two-step cascade starts with metal-free, fluorenone-catalyzed visible-light cleavage of α-methylstyrenes into prochiral ketones, then hands off to an alcohol dehydrogenase for the reduction. Swap the enzyme and you swap which enantiomer of the 1-arylalkan-1-ol comes out, so the stereochemistry is set by the biocatalyst, not the photochemistry.

original_title: Redox-Divergent Reactivity of a Gallium(I) Ambiphile toward an Allene, a Diyne, and Ph3PCN2
title: A low-valent gallium that mostly declines to get oxidized
blurb: Low-valent main-group metals are supposed to do oxidative addition, that's the whole point of them. This gallanediyl mostly doesn't: with an allene and a diyne it runs clean 1,2-syn carbometalation, keeping its oxidation state and single-bond character intact. Only with the diazophosphorus ylide Ph3PCN2 does it finally take the oxidative cycloaddition route. The interesting result is the exception, not the rule.

original_title: Energy Transfer Photocatalytic Carboamination of Alkenes toward Primary Amine-Derivatized Trifluoromethyl Ketals
title: One reagent, two handles: amine and trifluoromethyl ketone onto an alkene at once
blurb: A bifunctional reagent carrying both a trifluoromethyl ketal and an imine lets energy-transfer photocatalysis (thioxanthone, no metal) add a primary amine and a CF3 ketone across an alkene in one shot. Runs in continuous flow too, so they're clearly thinking past a single flask.

original_title: Reductive Sulfinyl Smiles–Truce Rearrangement of α-Bromoamides to α-Aryl Quaternary Centers
title: Building quaternary carbons by making a radical steal its own aryl group
blurb: Visible-light reduction of α-bromo N-acyl sulfinamides kicks out α-carbonyl radicals that yank the aryl group off a neighboring sulfinamide via Smiles-Truce rearrangement, landing quaternary α-aryl amide centers. Organic photocatalyst, operationally simple, and it handles both ring and open-chain substrates plus a range of (hetero)arenes and amide substituents.

original_title: Regioselective Copper-Catalyzed Acylsilylation of Allenes Using Acyl Fluorides
title: Acyl fluorides are the trick that makes allene acylsilylation actually work
blurb: CuOAc/PCy3 stitches acyl fluorides, allenes, and silylboranes together in one pot to give β-silyl unsaturated ketones with crowded quaternary carbons. The acyl fluoride specifically is what keeps the coupling productive; swap in a less reactive acyl donor and the reaction just detours into silaboration instead.

original_title: Activating the Gate-Opening Effect in Multivariate MOFs by Defect Engineering for Oxidative Desulfurization
title: Punching bigger holes in MOF pores by breaking them on purpose
blurb: Swapping in sulfonated linkers deliberately creates linker vacancies in a multivariate MOF, fusing pores open to 14.8 Å instead of leaving reactants stuck outside the usual cramped channels. That defect engineering alone is good for a 1.8-fold bump in dibenzothiophene oxidative desulfurization.

original_title: Synthesis of Highly Active InGaO X Solid Solution Catalysts and Their Superior Performance for CO 2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
title: Tuning indium oxide's methanol chemistry by dialing in gallium
blurb: A one-step hydrothermal synthesis makes InGaOx solid solutions across a range of Ga contents, and there's a sweet spot where the gallium reshapes the surface oxygen chemistry and redox behavior enough to lift CO2-to-methanol activity above plain indium oxide catalysts.

original_title: Optimization of patient dose and image quality for positron emission tomography-computed tomography
title: Dialing in the dose-versus-image-quality tradeoff for PET-CT
blurb: Optimizing patient radiation dose against image quality for PET-CT imaging protocols.

original_title: Partially Biobased Polyurethanes With Reversibly Crosslinkable Furan Units Toward Recyclable Thermosetting Textile Fibres
title: Textile fibers that can be un-crosslinked when you're done with them
blurb: A lignin-derived aromatic monomer gives the rigid backbone for partially biobased polyurethanes, copolymerized with flexible tetraethylene glycol and diisocyanates, with furan units wired in so the crosslinks can be reversed. The pitch is thermoset textile fibers that don't have to be landfill-only once they're cured.

original_title: Aligning H2 Activation with Functional-Group Polarity: K+-Promoted Switchable Hydrogenation on Pd/TiO2
title: Add potassium to a palladium catalyst and it starts hydrogenating C=O too
blurb: Plain Pd/TiO2 hydrogenates only the C=C bond of maleic anhydride, 99% selective to succinic anhydride. Dope it with K+ and the same catalyst suddenly takes the C=O bond as well, running clean to γ-butyrolactone at 99% selectivity. Same metal, same support, opposite chemoselectivity, just by changing how H2 splits.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Trifunctional Catalysis via Oxalate Supported Pt−Fe Dual Atoms to Break Site Spatial Restriction in Heterogeneous Catalytic Alkyne Hydrosilylation
title: Two metal atoms, one site, better odds at alkyne hydrosilylation
blurb: A Pt-Fe dual-atom catalyst on an oxalate-chelated support gets around the usual problem with single-site heterogeneous catalysts, that one isolated metal atom can't handle multiple substrate activation steps or steric bulk. Pairing the two atoms up lifts both activity and Markovnikov selectivity across internal and terminal alkynes.

original_title: NiH Catalysis-Enabled Synthesis of 4-Arylpiperidines from Pyridines and Aryl Iodides
title: 4-Arylpiperidines straight from pyridines and aryl iodides
blurb: NiH-catalyzed regioselective hydroarylation of 1,2-dihydropyridines installs the aryl group at C4, giving 4-aryl tetrahydropyridines that carry on to full piperidines via hydrogenation or further tweaking of the enamine. Aryl iodides and pyridines are about as common as reagents get, for a motif that shows up constantly in drugs.

original_title: Evidence for the Formation of an Iron(III)-Indolenylperoxo Intermediate During Indole Dioxygenation: Similarities with Heme Dioxygenases
title: Caught the peroxo intermediate mid-indole-dioxygenation
blurb: A synthetic iron(III)-porphyrin indolenylperoxo adduct trapped at -78°C and nailed down by UV-vis, EPR and Mössbauer, made either from FeIII(TPP)(Cl) plus O2, methoxide and 3-methylindole, or from a preformed iron-superoxo complex reacting with the same substrate. It's the same kind of intermediate heme dioxygenases like IDO and TDO are thought to use, just parked in a model porphyrin where you can actually watch it sit still.

original_title: Self-assembled iridium(III) photosensitizers induce cuproptosis without copper supplementation for efficient anticancer therapy
title: An iridium photosensitizer that triggers cuproptosis without adding copper
blurb: Self-assembled Ir(III) complexes act as photosensitizers that push cancer cells into cuproptosis, the copper-dependent death pathway, without needing to dose in extra copper to get there.

original_title: PSMA PET Imaging for Radioligand Therapy Selection Across Prostate Cancer Disease States - Steve Cho - UroToday
title: PSMA PET as the gatekeeper for radioligand therapy
blurb: Steve Cho on how PSMA PET imaging factors into picking which prostate cancer patients get radioligand therapy, across disease states from localized to metastatic castration-resistant.

original_title: Solvent-Controlled Remote Chemodivergent Synthesis of γ,δ-/γ-Functionalization of 2 H -Chromen-2-ones via Cascade 1,6-Conjugate Additions
title: Same coumarin substrate, two different products, just swap the solvent
blurb: Cascade 1,6-conjugate additions of cyanoalkenyl coumarins with bromomalonates fork on solvent alone: dichloromethane drives a cyclopropanation route to polysubstituted cyclopropane-coumarins in up to 90% yield with >25:1 dr, while ethyl acetate triggers cyclization/ring-opening instead, giving (Z)-styrylcoumarins. Same starting materials, solvent decides the scaffold.

original_title: Organocatalyzed Asymmetric Formal [3+2] Cycloaddition between Cyclic Nitrones and Meldrum’s Acid for the Formal Total Synthesis of (−)-Crispine A
title: A quinine-derived catalyst threads the needle to (-)-crispine A
blurb: An asymmetric formal [3+2] cycloaddition between cyclic nitrones and Meldrum's acid, run with a quinine-derived amine-urea organocatalyst, gives an optically active isoxazolidinone that feeds into a known precursor of (-)-crispine A. It's a formal synthesis riding on that precursor's established endgame, but the organocatalytic step is the new piece.

original_title: Synthesis of adaptive 15N-nitrosyl-Co7 nanocluster for electrocatalytic C–H functionalization
title: Teaching a Co7 nanocluster to flex its NO ligands so it doesn't fall apart
blurb: Nanoclusters usually trade stability for catalytic activity. Here the adaptive coordination of NO ligands lets a Co7 cluster hold onto both for electrocatalytic C-H functionalization, and a 15N-labeling trick is what actually lets them pin down the nitrosyl-Co7 structure and mechanism instead of just guessing at one.

original_title: A Proton-Responsive Backbone Relay for Selective Two-Electron Oxygen Reduction to H2O2
title: Editing a polymer's backbone after the fact to make it hand out protons on cue
blurb: Photocatalytic H2O2 production usually needs charge separation, O2 activation and proton delivery tuned separately. A postsynthetic thiol-yne edit turns a previously inert alkynyl bridge in a donor-acceptor covalent organic polymer into a proton-responsive module, swapping in -SCH2COOH groups so proton delivery is wired directly into the catalytic site instead of optimized on the side.

original_title: Scalable Iron-Catalyzed Radical Bromochlorination of Alkenes with HCl under Thermal Conditions
title: Bromochlorinating alkenes in a minute flat with just iron and HCl
blurb: Cheap HCl pulls double duty, activating NBS to generate the bromine radical and supplying the chlorine, while Fe(III)-Cl shuttles the chlorine atom over via radical ligand transfer. Plain thermal conditions, done in a minute, and it scales to multigram, which is the part that actually matters for a halogenation method.

original_title: Four-Electron Reduction of O2 at a Single Metal Center: Redox Chemistry of a Uranium(II) Synthon
title: This 'uranium(II)' reduction actually happened on the ligand
blurb: One-electron reduction of a U(III) arene complex reads like it should land on the metal, but the product's structure tells a different story: the arene ring is badly distorted in a way consistent with it absorbing the electrons, while the metal center gets pushed up to formally U(IV) to balance the books. So the electron count lies about where the redox chemistry actually happened, on the way to building a synthon meant for four-electron O2 reduction.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Electrochemical Formal Amidation of Benzyl Halides via Radical-Polar Crossover
title: Turning benzyl halides into amides using the solvent as the amine source
blurb: Electrochemical radical-polar crossover converts benzyl halides straight to N-substituted acetamides, with acetonitrile doing double duty as solvent and amidation reagent, Ritter-style, and a diphenyl disulfide radical shuttle carrying the process along. No metal, no external oxidant, and paired electrolysis so both electrodes are doing real work instead of one just babysitting the other.

original_title: Metal–Support Interfaces in Pt1/γ-Al2O3 Single Atom Catalysts with Atomic-Level Precision
title: Finally mapping what's actually holding the platinum atom to the alumina
blurb: Single atom catalysts get sold on maxing out every metal atom's usefulness, but for the model Pt1/γ-Al2O3 system, the chemical nature of the Pt-support interface has stayed murky. This pins it down at atomic resolution, which matters more than usual here since the interface basically is the catalyst when your active site is one atom.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Engineering Nonpathogenic Bacteria for Synergistic Tumor-Targeted Protein Degradation and Immunotherapy by Checkpoint-Inhibiting Nanobodies
title: Bacteria that hand-deliver a protein degrader and a checkpoint blocker on the same schedule
blurb: An engineered nonpathogenic bacterial platform uses its own metabolism to time two things at once: displaying tumor-targeted protein degradation chimeras on its surface via bioorthogonal click chemistry, and secreting checkpoint-inhibiting nanobodies. The point is synchrony, degradation and immune activation hitting the tumor together instead of on separate schedules.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Symmetry-Guided Optical Control of Dynamic 1D Protein Self-Assembly and Precise In Vitro Initiation of Biomolecular Condensation.
title: Light as the on-switch for protein self-assembly
blurb: Uses symmetry rules to optically steer proteins into ordered 1D chains and to trigger biomolecular condensation in vitro with defined timing.

original_title: Omics-scale capture of electrophilic metabolites
title: A probe that catches the reactive metabolites everyone else's methods lose
blurb: Most metabolic intermediates are electrophilic and short-lived, coenzyme-A esters, ketones, aldehydes, and standard metabolomics mostly just misses them. TAMOHA is a nucleophilic hydroxylamine probe that tags these species so they actually show up in the data instead of disappearing during workup.

original_title: Improved Native Top-Down Characterization of Protein Complexes Afforded by Cyclic Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry
title: Cyclic ion mobility gets native top-down MS further into big protein complexes
blurb: Native top-down MS should read out proteoform-level detail on intact complexes, but sequence coverage on large assemblies has been the limiting factor. Adding cyclic ion mobility separation ahead of fragmentation pushes that coverage up.

original_title: Replaying germinal center evolution on a quantified affinity landscape
title: Rerunning the germinal center to see if affinity maturation is predictable
blurb: A parallel replay experiment starts germinal center B cells from the same point and runs them side by side. The affinity gains aren't noise, they follow predictable evolutionary forces, which is a decent argument that affinity maturation is more law than chance.

original_title: Repositioning Proton and Electron Donors in a Family of Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer Mediators
title: Does the bridge in a PCET mediator actually do anything
blurb: Reductive PCET reagents typically tether an acid and a reductant with a connecting group to cut the effective molecularity, but what that bridge does to the thermodynamics and kinetics hasn't been tested systematically. Four anilinium-cobaltocene mediators, one made via late-stage Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling on a cobaltocenium salt, let them vary the bridge and clock PCET rates to aryl ketones directly.

original_title: The Tetrahedron Speaks: A Holistic Benchmark for DFT in Tetrahedral Framework
title: Average Si-O bond length is a bad way to grade DFT on zeolites
blurb: Thirty years of DFT benchmarking on zeolites and other tetrahedral frameworks has leaned on mean Si-O bond length as the accuracy check. Averaging lets local overestimates and underestimates cancel each other out, so a functional can nail that one number while getting the actual framework geometry wrong.

original_title: Theoretical Study on the Rh(III)-Catalyzed [5 + 1] Annulation of 2-Alkenylanilide and Allenyl Acetate
title: Working out why the Rh(III) [5+1] annulation goes where it goes
blurb: A DFT mechanism study on the Rh(III)-catalyzed [5+1] annulation of 2-alkenylanilide with allenyl acetate. RhCp*(SbF6)2 turns out to be the actual catalyst, and after acetate coordination and N-H activation set the stage, the turnover-determining step is the C-C coupling, with a 26.3 kcal/mol barrier.

original_title: Biomass-Derived Cooperative Pyridinic/Pyrrolic-N Sites Enable Efficient Metal-Free N-Alkylation of Alcohols with Amines
title: Chitosan char doing a metal catalyst's job on N-alkylation
blurb: Carbon microspheres made from chitosan, loaded with tunable pyridinic and pyrrolic nitrogen sites, catalyze N-alkylation of alcohols with amines under mild conditions with no metal involved, sidestepping the leaching and poisoning issues that plague the usual metal catalysts for this reaction.

original_title: ITM neuroendocrine tumor drug spurned by FDA over manufacturing qualms
title: ITM's neuroendocrine tumor drug rejected over how it's made, not what it does
blurb: The FDA turned down ITM Isotopes' lead radiopharmaceutical for neuroendocrine tumors, and the problem isn't efficacy or safety, it's manufacturing. Usually the more fixable kind of rejection, but it still means a delay and another round with the agency before this reaches anyone.

original_title: An All-Solid-State Calcium Ion-Selective Electrode with a Peptide-Based Interface Integrating Passive Antifouling and Active Photothermal Bactericidal Strategies for Long-Term Seawater Monitoring
title: A calcium electrode that kills its own biofilm
blurb: An all-solid-state Ca2+ electrode coated in phytic acid, Prussian blue nanoparticles, and an antimicrobial peptide, self-assembled into an interface that's hydrophilic enough to resist fouling and photothermal enough to actively cook off whatever sticks anyway. Built for long-term seawater monitoring, where biofouling normally kills sensor stability within weeks.

original_title: Innate Pharma Announces Completion of Enrollment in Phase 1 Dose Escalation Study of IPH4502, a Novel Nectin-4 Exatecan Antibody-drug Conjugate (ADC) - Yahoo Finance
title: Innate Pharma's Nectin-4 ADC finishes filling its dose-escalation cohort
blurb: Enrollment is complete for the Phase 1 dose-escalation trial of IPH4502, Innate Pharma's Nectin-4-targeted, exatecan-loaded ADC. No efficacy or safety data yet, just the box checked that lets dose-finding actually start reading out.

original_title: Hydrogel formulation controls size-dependent accumulation of proteins and nanoparticles in PEG microparticles
title: Tuning hydrogel pores for cargo bigger than the usual small-molecule probes
blurb: Hydrogel permeability is normally characterized with small molecules, but the payloads people actually want in, protein conjugates and nanoparticles, are much larger. This runs a 36-condition PEG-acrylate microparticle formulation matrix and tracks accumulation across that size range, giving an actual size-dependent map instead of extrapolating from small-molecule data.

original_title: Elucidating the Mechanism of Photoinduced Sulfur Monoxide Extrusion from Dianthryl Sulfoxide
title: Working out how light strips sulfur monoxide out of a sulfoxide to forge a C–C bond
blurb: 9,9'-Dianthryl sulfoxide loses SO under light and the two anthryl groups fuse into a new C–C bond. This paper pins down the mechanism behind that extrusion, relevant to anyone building complex skeletons via fragment elimination instead of standard coupling chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
